# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 60 (Bi-Vb Pc60)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc60
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 60
**Title (English, from literature):** Getting medical treatment from a man
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 60, titled *Pasākhejāta*, establishes a pācittiya offense for a nun who is alone with a man and receives medical treatment from him on the thigh or lower body [Hüsken 1997]. As observed by Ute Hüsken, this regulation is unique to nuns and has no direct counterpart in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga [Hüsken 1997]. The offense entails having a solitary man lance, open, wash, rub, bandage, or remove the dressing from an affliction situated below the navel and above the knees [Hüsken 1997]. In the Vinaya commentary, the *Samantapāsādikā* (Sp 939) explains the term *pasākhe* as referring to the lower body (*adhokāye*), noting that the two thighs branch out from that region like the branches of a tree (*rukkhassa sākhā viya ubho ūrā pabhijjitvā gatā*) [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation of the rule and its origin story is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Curated parallels include the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Bhikkhunī Parivāra (both Pc 60), as well as Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha rules preserved in Chinese for the Dharmaguptaka (Pc 147), Mahīśāsaka (Pc 168), Sarvāstivāda (Pc 162/163), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Pc 159), and Mahāsaṅghika (Pc 133) recensions; in Tibetan for the Mūlasarvāstivāda (Pc 108); and in Sanskrit for the Mahāsaṅghika-Lokottaravāda (Pc 133). Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records 472 textual reuses across 96 texts, featuring extensive formulaic sharing with Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 3, Pācittiyas 11, 14, and 13, and the Katāpattivāra of the Parivāra [DharmaNexus].
